src/services/qiCardPaymentService.ts.whatsWrong: The validation guard on L72 (`if (!data?.formUrl && !data?.paymentId && !tokenOptions?.paymentToken)`) is intended to allow instant-SUCCESS token payments that legitimately have no formUrl. But because `!tokenOptions?.paymentToken` short-circuits the whole condition to false whenever a paymentToken is supplied, ALL validation is skipped in the token path — including genuine error responses. On L76 the payload is then `return data as QiCardPaymentResult`, so a server error object or null is returned as a 'successful' result. Note the normal (no-token) path IS safe: null data trips the guard and throws.
src/services/qiCardPaymentService.ts.rootCause: The single AND-chained guard conflates 'formUrl may be legitimately absent for token payments' with 'skip validation entirely for token payments'. It never independently checks for an explicit server error field or for null data.
src/services/qiCardPaymentService.ts.failureScenario: User pays with a saved QiCard token. Edge Function returns HTTP 200 with body `{ error: 'payment token expired' }` (so supabase's top-level `error` is null and L64 doesn't fire). L72 evaluates `true && true && false` = false, so no throw. L76 returns `{ error: 'payment token expired' }` cast as QiCardPaymentResult. The caller treats it as success: reads `result.status`/`result.formUrl` (both undefined) — WebView gets an undefined URL or the order is marked paid though QiCard charged nothing, and the real error is never surfaced to the user. If data is null (function returned 204/empty) the same path returns null and the caller crashes on `result.status`.

src/services/qiCardPaymentService.ts.whatsWrong: pollForCompletion exposes no way to be cancelled. With maxAttempts=10 and backoff capped at 8s, a payment stuck in CREATED keeps the loop alive for ~60s of cumulative sleeps plus request time, with no AbortSignal to break out.
src/services/qiCardPaymentService.ts.rootCause: The polling loop only terminates on a terminal status, an exhausted attempt count, or a final-attempt throw. There is no signal parameter and the `await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(...))` sleeps are not abortable.
src/services/qiCardPaymentService.ts.failureScenario: On a slow Iraqi mobile connection the payment stays CREATED. The user backgrounds the app or navigates away from the checkout screen. pollForCompletion keeps running for up to ~60s and finally resolves/rejects, at which point the (unmounted) checkout screen calls setState on the result — React 'update on unmounted component' warning at best, and needless battery/network burn while backgrounded. Callers cannot stop it because the service offers no cancel handle.

src/services/storeProfileService.ts.whatsWrong: The service caches profiles for 10 minutes (profileCache per-tenant, line 68; allStoresCache, line 70) but NEITHER updateStoreProfile (successful write at line 183) NOR setDefaultLocation (write at line 223) invalidates those caches. There is no clearCache method anywhere in the codebase. After a write, the next getStoreProfile / getAllStoreProfiles returns stale pre-edit data for up to 10 minutes.
src/services/storeProfileService.ts.rootCause: Write methods mutate Supabase directly and never touch this.profileCache / this.allStoresCache, so the in-memory cache diverges from the DB.
src/services/storeProfileService.ts.failureScenario: Admin opens store settings, renames store from 'Ali Store' to 'Ali Electronics' and taps Save. updateStoreProfile succeeds, AdminStoreProfileScreen (line 487-491) shows 'saved successfully' and navigates back. The customer-facing StoreProductsScreen and the admin's own re-entry both call getStoreProfile(tenantId), which returns the CACHED old profile 'Ali Store' for up to 10 min. Admin thinks the save failed and re-saves repeatedly; customers browsing getAllStoreProfiles see the old name/logo/cover for 10 min. A cover/logo image swap via AdminDashboardScreen (lines 130/156) shows the old image the same way.

src/services/storeProfileService.ts.whatsWrong: setDefaultLocation performs `await supabase.from('tenants').update(updateData).eq('id', tenantId);` but never destructures or checks the returned `error`. A failed write (RLS/permission denied, network drop, constraint violation) resolves as success. This is inconsistent with updateStoreProfile (line 183-188) which correctly checks and throws.
src/services/storeProfileService.ts.rootCause: The `{ error }` result of the Supabase update is discarded; the promise resolving is treated as write success even though supabase-js resolves (does not reject) on DB-level errors.
src/services/storeProfileService.ts.failureScenario: Admin picks a store location and saves. AdminStoreProfileScreen line 484 calls setDefaultLocation. The tenants UPDATE fails (e.g. transient network loss or RLS), but no error is thrown, so control returns to line 487 and shows 'Store profile saved successfully' then navigates back. The location was never persisted, yet the admin believes it was — public_location_id / address_text / city stay unset and the store shows no location to customers, with no indication anything went wrong.
src/services/storeProfileService.ts.fix: Capture and throw the error like the other write path: `const { error } = await supabase.from('tenants').update(updateData).eq('id', tenantId); if (error) { console.error('setDefaultLocation failed:', error); throw error; }`

src/services/storeProfileService.ts.whatsWrong: The operating_hours merge does a read-modify-write but the SELECT only destructures `{ data: existingData }` — its error is ignored. If that select errors transiently, existingData is undefined, so `{ ...(existingData?.operating_hours || {}), ...hours }` collapses to just the partial `hours` being written, silently DROPPING previously-saved operating_hours fields not present in this update.
src/services/storeProfileService.ts.rootCause: Non-atomic read-modify-write whose read failure is indistinguishable from an empty result, combined with the merge treating a failed read as 'no existing hours'.
src/services/storeProfileService.ts.failureScenario: A tenant has operating_hours = { openTime, closeTime, closedDays, timeZone } saved. Admin edits only openTime (data.openTime set, other hours fields undefined so `hours` = { openTime }). The `select('operating_hours')` on line 179 fails transiently (network blip). existingData is undefined, so line 180 writes operating_hours = { openTime } — closeTime, closedDays and timeZone are wiped from the DB with no error surfaced.
src/services/storeProfileService.ts.fix: Check the read error and abort rather than merging into an empty object: `const { data: existingData, error: readErr } = await supabase.from('tenants').select('operating_hours').eq('id', tenantId).single(); if (readErr) throw readErr; updateData.operating_hours = { ...(existingData?.operating_hours || {}), ...hours };` (ideally move the merge server-side / into a single RPC to make it atomic, but at minimum stop silently discarding existing fields on a failed read).

src/services/tenantAdminService.ts.whatsWrong: updateSettings() never inspects the upsert result's `error`. Supabase does NOT throw on DB errors — it returns { error }. The try/catch only catches thrown JS/network exceptions, so any DB-level failure (RLS denial, constraint, or the request failing after send) resolves as SUCCESS. This is the single writer behind saveSettings, partner_links, and the entire partner ledger, all of which silently believe the write persisted.
src/services/tenantAdminService.ts.rootCause: Result destructured without `error`; unlike every other write method in this file which does `if (error) throw error`.
src/services/tenantAdminService.ts.failureScenario: Owner on a flaky Iraqi mobile connection taps Save on Invoice Settings (AdminInvoiceSettingsScreen:195 → saveSettings → updateSettings), or records a $500 partner cash deposit via addPartnerLedgerEntry. The upsert round-trip returns { error } (e.g. RLS/connection drop). Method resolves cleanly, UI shows 'Saved', but nothing was written — the deposit / invoice settings / new partner link vanish on next reload with zero error surfaced.
src/services/tenantAdminService.ts.fix: const { error } = await supabase.from('tenant_settings').upsert({ tenant_id: this.tenantId, setting_key: settingId, setting_value: settingData, updated_at: new Date().toISOString() }, { onConflict: 'tenant_id, setting_key' }); if (error) throw error;

src/services/tenantAdminService.ts.whatsWrong: updateOrderStatus deducts/restores stock via a non-atomic read-modify-write: it reads currentStockStatus, computes requiresDeduction/requiresRestore, calls moveStockForItems, THEN writes stock_status — with no conditional/in-flight guard. Two concurrent calls both read the pre-write stock_status and both move stock. (Separately, the order read on line 678 is not tenant-scoped — `.eq('id', orderId).single()` with no tenant_id — relying purely on RLS.)
src/services/tenantAdminService.ts.rootCause: The stock_status guard is meant to make the transition idempotent but is applied as read-then-write, not as an atomic conditional update, so concurrent readers both pass it.
src/services/tenantAdminService.ts.failureScenario: Admin double-taps 'Mark as Delivered' in AdminOrdersScreen (or two staff act on the same pending order from two phones). Call A reads stock_status='pending' → deduct; before A commits, call B also reads 'pending' → deduct. A 3-unit order deducts 6 units → stock underflows toward 0 and the shop oversells. Symmetric double-restore on a double-tapped cancel over-credits inventory.
src/services/tenantAdminService.ts.fix: Claim the transition atomically before moving stock: const { data: claimed } = await supabase.from('orders').update({ stock_status: requiresDeduction ? 'deducted' : 'rolled_back', status, updated_at: new Date().toISOString() }).eq('id', orderId).eq('tenant_id', this.tenantId).eq('stock_status', currentStockStatus).select('id'); if (claimed?.length) await this.moveStockForItems(order.items || [], requiresDeduction ? 'deduct' : 'restore'); — only move stock when the guarded UPDATE actually claimed the row (ideally a SECURITY DEFINER RPC).

src/services/tenantAdminService.ts.whatsWrong: returnOrderItems restores stock and recomputes totals via read-modify-write with no atomic claim or in-flight lock. The index/productId validation guards against the order CHANGING between reads, but not against two simultaneous returns that both read the same original state.
src/services/tenantAdminService.ts.rootCause: No optimistic-concurrency check (updated_at) or server-side atomic path around the restore + total recompute.
src/services/tenantAdminService.ts.failureScenario: Admin double-taps 'Confirm Return' (or two devices). Both reads see the original order.items, both pass the index validation, both call moveStockForItems('restore') for the same units → stock is credited twice. The final order UPDATE is last-write-wins so items/total shrink only once, leaving physical inventory overstated by the returned quantity, and both callers report a refund to the operator.
src/services/tenantAdminService.ts.fix: Gate the restore behind an atomic claim — re-check `updated_at` unchanged in the final UPDATE (`.eq('updated_at', order.updated_at)`) and only run moveStockForItems('restore') if that guarded UPDATE reported a changed row; or move the whole operation into a SECURITY DEFINER RPC. Add an in-flight guard in the caller as a stopgap.

src/ui/androidGlobalFix.ts.whatsWrong: The ENTIRE function is inert on RN 0.81 / React 19.1. Verified in node_modules: both `Text` (TextImpl) and `TextInput` are declared as plain FUNCTION components (`const TextInput = function TextInput({ ref, ... })`, `component()` is only a Flow type). React 19 removed `defaultProps` support for function components — it IGNORES `Text.defaultProps` and `TextInput.defaultProps` entirely (and logs a one-time 'Support for defaultProps will be removed from function components' dev warning per component). Separately, because TextInput is a plain function, `TextInput.prototype.render` is `undefined`, so the `if (originalRender)` render-patch (lines 48-62) never installs and control always falls to the fallback on lines 66-71 — which ALSO writes `TextInput.defaultProps.style`, equally ignored. Net: `allowFontScaling` is NOT disabled, `scrollEnabled` is NOT set, and none of the `includeFontPadding`/`textAlignVertical`/`paddingVertical` style fixes apply.
src/ui/androidGlobalFix.ts.rootCause: Patch was written for the pre-React-19 world where function components still honored `defaultProps` and class components had `prototype.render`. RN 0.81 migrated Text/TextInput to React-19 function components (ref-as-prop), invalidating both mechanisms.
src/ui/androidGlobalFix.ts.failureScenario: Samsung/low-RAM Android user sets OS font size to Huge and uses Arabic/Kurdish. Because allowFontScaling stays true (default), bold Arabic scales up and clips horizontally/vertically inside buttons and price rows — the exact bug this file was written to prevent. In dev, the console is also spammed with React 19 defaultProps-deprecation warnings for every Text/TextInput.
src/ui/androidGlobalFix.ts.fix: Stop relying on `defaultProps` and `prototype.render`. Replace with a mechanism React 19 actually honors, e.g. wrap the components: `const OrigTextRender = Text.render; ...` no longer applies, so instead reassign the exports to wrapper functions that inject the props, or (simplest, app-wide) route all text through a custom `AppText`/`AppTextInput` that hardcodes `allowFontScaling={false}` and the fix styles. If keeping a global monkeypatch, override via `Object.assign` on a wrapper: `const Base = Text; const Patched = (p) => Base({ allowFontScaling: false, textBreakStrategy: 'simple', ...p, style: [{ includeFontPadding: true, textAlignVertical: 'center' }, p.style] }); export`… — and verify with a runtime assertion/dev log that the injected props reach the native component.

src/ui/androidGlobalFix.ts.whatsWrong: `textBreakStrategy: 'simple'` is placed inside the `style` object. `textBreakStrategy` is a Text PROP (`'simple' | 'highQuality' | 'balanced'`), not a TextStyle field, so it is silently dropped when nested in a style — even on an RN/React version where defaultProps.style worked. The comment calls it the 'CRITICAL FIX' for horizontal cutoff, but as written it does nothing.
src/ui/androidGlobalFix.ts.rootCause: Confusing Android layout props with style properties.
src/ui/androidGlobalFix.ts.failureScenario: Even if the defaultProps mechanism were restored (fix for the S1 finding), long Arabic strings would still get RN's default `highQuality` break strategy and clip, because the intended `simple` strategy never reaches the component from inside a style object.
src/ui/androidGlobalFix.ts.fix: Move it out of style into a prop: `Text.defaultProps.textBreakStrategy = 'simple';` (or, in the wrapper approach from the S1 fix, pass `textBreakStrategy="simple"` as a prop). Keep only `includeFontPadding` and `textAlignVertical` inside the style array.

src/ui/patchPressable.ts.whatsWrong: defaultProps supplies a prop value ONLY when that prop is `undefined`; it substitutes, it never merges. Because `style` is a single prop, any `<TouchableOpacity style={...}>` or `<Pressable style={...}>` — i.e. essentially every button in the app — passes its own `style`, so `defaultProps.style` (the `safeStyle` carrying minHeight:44 / paddingVertical:6) is discarded entirely. The safe style is applied ONLY to touchables that render with no `style` prop at all, which almost none do. The patch therefore does not deliver the minHeight/padding it exists to provide.
src/ui/patchPressable.ts.rootCause: Misuse of defaultProps as if it deep-merges style; it does not. A default prop is used only in place of an absent prop, so a per-component style prop fully shadows the injected safeStyle instead of layering under it.
src/ui/patchPressable.ts.failureScenario: On a Samsung device at max OS font size in Arabic, a button coded as `<TouchableOpacity style={styles.btn}>` (styles.btn has height:36 or no minHeight) still clips its scaled Arabic label vertically — exactly the bug this file claims to fix — because safeStyle is never merged into the styled button.
src/ui/patchPressable.ts.fix: Stop relying on defaultProps for style layering. Provide the safe base via wrapper components that compose it under the caller's style, e.g. export patched touchables: `export const SafePressable = forwardRef((props, ref) => <Pressable ref={ref} {...props} style={[safeStyle, props.style]} />)` (and likewise for TouchableOpacity), then migrate call sites; or apply the minHeight/paddingVertical directly in the shared button component(s). The array-merge must happen at render time on the resolved `style` prop, not via defaultProps.

src/ui/patchPressable.ts.whatsWrong: React 19 (this app's version) removed `defaultProps` support for function components. `Pressable` is a forwardRef/function component, so assigning `(Pressable as any).defaultProps` is silently ignored by React 19 — the Pressable half of this patch has zero effect even for a style-less Pressable. (TouchableOpacity is still a class component so its defaultProps is at least read, but is neutralized by the substitution bug above.)
src/ui/patchPressable.ts.rootCause: The header comment claims defaultProps is a 'stable API', but React 19 dropped defaultProps for function components; Pressable is exactly such a component, so the assignment is dead code under this stack.
src/ui/patchPressable.ts.failureScenario: Any Pressable-based control (the modern RN button primitive) gets none of the minHeight/padding on Android; at max font size its content is clipped and the touch target can fall below 44dp, with no warning that the patch did nothing.
src/ui/patchPressable.ts.fix: Do not patch Pressable via defaultProps under React 19. Use the wrapper-component approach from the previous finding (SafePressable applying `style={[safeStyle, props.style]}`) so the safe base is composed at render time, which works regardless of function-vs-class component.

src/ui/patchTextInput.ts.whatsWrong: scrollEnabled: props.scrollEnabled ?? false is applied to ALL TextInputs, including multiline ones. RN defaults multiline scrollEnabled to true precisely so users can scroll within a height-capped growing input. Forcing it false disables internal scrolling for every multiline input that doesn't explicitly re-enable it. Confirmed live: src/screens/messenger/ChatThreadScreen.tsx lines 291-308 render a `multiline` chat composer inside a container capped at maxHeight:120 (style line 395) and never passes scrollEnabled — so this patch forces it off.
src/ui/patchTextInput.ts.rootCause: The patch was designed for single-line bounce suppression but branches on nothing — multiline is a first-class TextInput mode that needs scrolling.
src/ui/patchTextInput.ts.failureScenario: On a 320dp low-RAM Android at max OS font size, an Arabic/Kurdish user composes a long chat message. After ~4-5 lines the input reaches its 120dp maxHeight; with scrollEnabled:false the content view can no longer scroll to follow the caret, so the text being typed and the earlier lines are clipped out of view and cannot be scrolled back to for review or editing. The same applies to address (AddEditAddress uses multiline) and admin notification composers. The input becomes effectively unusable for anything longer than the visible box.
src/ui/patchTextInput.ts.fix: Preserve RN's multiline default instead of clobbering it: `scrollEnabled: props.multiline ? props.scrollEnabled : (props.scrollEnabled ?? false),` (apply the same guard at line 58 in the fallback branch).

src/hooks/usePushRegistration.ts.whatsWrong: The useEffect guards only `!isNativeAvailable || !getMessagingFn` (line 170), then calls `getMessagingFn()` (line 174) and `onTokenRefreshFn!(msg, ...)` (line 175) with NO try/catch and WITHOUT checking `onTokenRefreshFn`. This is inconsistent with registerNativePushToken, where the author deliberately wrapped the identical `getMessagingFn()` call in try/catch (line 39-40). `isNativeAvailable` is set purely because the JS `require('@react-native-firebase/messaging')` succeeded (line 16-24) — it does NOT prove the native Firebase app is initialized, nor that every modular export (`onTokenRefresh`) exists in the installed version.
src/hooks/usePushRegistration.ts.rootCause: `isNativeAvailable` conflates 'JS module bundled' with 'native module usable'. The effect trusts the non-null assertion `onTokenRefreshFn!` and the throw-capable `getMessaging()` without the try/catch that the sibling function has.
src/hooks/usePushRegistration.ts.failureScenario: On a build where the JS module is bundled but the default Firebase app failed to initialize (e.g. a preview/EAS build with the google-services plugin misconfigured), `getMessaging()` throws `No Firebase App '[DEFAULT]' has been created` at line 174. OR: an @react-native-firebase version where the modular `onTokenRefresh` export is absent leaves `onTokenRefreshFn` null while `getMessagingFn` is set, so `onTokenRefreshFn!(...)` throws `not a function` at line 175. Either throw happens inside the useEffect callback (uncaught) → React unwinds to the ErrorBoundary → app error screen instead of degrading gracefully the way registerNativePushToken does.
src/hooks/usePushRegistration.ts.fix: Wrap the native calls and guard the extra ref, mirroring registerNativePushToken: `useEffect(() => { if (!isNativeAvailable || !getMessagingFn || !onTokenRefreshFn) return; registerToken(); let unsubscribe: (() => void) | undefined; try { const msg = getMessagingFn(); unsubscribe = onTokenRefreshFn(msg, async (newToken: string) => { /* ...existing... */ }); } catch (e) { console.warn('FCM token-refresh subscription failed:', e); } return () => { try { unsubscribe?.(); } catch {} }; }, [registerToken]);`

src/services/addressService.ts.whatsWrong: deleteAddress() removes a row by id but never promotes a replacement default. If the user deletes the address whose is_default=true, every remaining address stays is_default=false, so the user ends up with addresses but NO default.
src/services/addressService.ts.rootCause: Delete only issues `.delete().eq('id', addressId)`; nothing checks whether the deleted row was the default nor promotes another. MyAddressScreen.handleDeleteAddress (line 135) also just filters local state, so it does not compensate.
src/services/addressService.ts.failureScenario: User has address A (default) and B. In MyAddressScreen they delete A. B remains with is_default=false. At checkout, addressService.getDefaultAddress(userId) returns null (CheckoutScreen line 260 / ChatScreen line 1125), so no delivery address is pre-selected and the user is told to 'add a delivery address first' even though B exists.

src/services/addressService.ts.whatsWrong: setDefaultAddress() (and the same pattern in addAddress lines 79-81/100 and updateAddress lines 116-118/136) clears is_default on ALL of the user's rows FIRST, then sets the new default. If the second write fails, the user is left with ZERO defaults.
src/services/addressService.ts.rootCause: removeDefaultFromOtherAddresses() runs before the `.update({ is_default: true })`. The two statements are not transactional, so a failure between them corrupts state.
src/services/addressService.ts.failureScenario: User taps 'Set as default' on address B; removeDefaultFromOtherAddresses clears A's default (succeeds), then the app is backgrounded / loses network and the line-157 update throws. DB now has no default at all. getDefaultAddress returns null at checkout even though A and B both exist. The thrown error shows a failure toast, but the corruption already happened.

src/services/addressService.ts.whatsWrong: updateAddress writes with `.update(updateData).eq('id', addressId)` — user_id is passed in but never used to scope the write. deleteAddress has no user_id at all. Supabase update/delete return `{ error: null }` when zero rows match, so the caller is told it succeeded even when nothing changed.
src/services/addressService.ts.rootCause: The write filter is id-only. This app is mid Firebase->Supabase migration; if RLS on `addresses` is disabled/misconfigured, any authenticated user can update/delete another user's row by id. Even with RLS enabled, an RLS-blocked or nonexistent-id update returns no error, so AddEditAddressScreen (line 590) still alerts 'address updated' though the DB is untouched.
src/services/addressService.ts.failureScenario: Edit flow: address.id no longer belongs to the user (stale nav param / row removed on another device). updateAddress issues the update, 0 rows match, no error thrown -> screen shows 'Address updated' success and navigates back, but nothing was saved. Worse without RLS: a crafted id lets one user overwrite/delete another user's address.

src/services/appConfigService.ts.whatsWrong: getAppConfig destructures `error` from the `.single()` result but never checks it. With `.single()`, a query-level failure (RLS denial, PostgREST 5xx, or the legitimate zero-rows case PGRST116) returns `{ data: null, error: <set> }` WITHOUT throwing, so control never reaches the catch. Line 122 then treats `data == null` as 'no config exists', builds DEFAULT_CONFIG, and line 123 caches DEFAULT_CONFIG for the full 1h TTL.
src/services/appConfigService.ts.rootCause: Conflating a transient query error with a genuinely empty table, plus caching the fallback.
src/services/appConfigService.ts.failureScenario: Server has forceUpdate=true (a broken build must be blocked). A transient RLS/PostgREST error returns error+null data. getAppConfig silently caches DEFAULT_CONFIG (forceUpdate=false) for 1 hour, so evaluateUpdate/checkForUpdate return mode 'none' and users on the broken build are NOT blocked for up to an hour, even after the backend recovers.
src/services/appConfigService.ts.fix: Use `.maybeSingle()` (returns data:null,error:null for zero rows) and surface real errors to the catch/stale-cache path: `const { data, error } = await supabase.from('app_config').select('data').eq('id', AppConfigService.DOCUMENT).maybeSingle(); if (error) throw error;` — the existing catch (L125-130) then falls back to the STALE cached config instead of overwriting it with DEFAULT.

src/services/appConfigService.ts.whatsWrong: normalizeConfig defaults the store URLs with `String(data?.androidStoreUrl ?? DEFAULT)`. Nullish coalescing (`??`) only fires on null/undefined, so an empty string from the server passes straight through, making androidStoreUrl/iosStoreUrl `''`. openStore then calls `Linking.canOpenURL('')` which resolves false, throws, and the throw propagates.
src/services/appConfigService.ts.rootCause: `??` does not catch empty strings; store URL (unlike updateMessage at L315 which uses `||`) has no non-empty guard downstream.
src/services/appConfigService.ts.failureScenario: An admin blanks the store URL field in the app_config editor (saved as ""). A user on an old build hits the FORCE-update modal (non-dismissible). They tap 'Update' -> openStore throws -> ForceUpdateModal.handleUpdate (L141-147) just logs and re-enables the button. The store never opens and the modal cannot be dismissed: the user is hard-locked out of the app with a button that does nothing.
src/services/appConfigService.ts.fix: Guard against empty strings in normalizeConfig: `androidStoreUrl: (typeof data?.androidStoreUrl === 'string' && data.androidStoreUrl.trim()) ? data.androidStoreUrl : DEFAULT_CONFIG.androidStoreUrl,` and the same for `iosStoreUrl`. (Optionally also fall back to DEFAULT_CONFIG URLs inside getStoreUrl before opening.)

src/services/appConfigService.ts.whatsWrong: minVersionCode/minBuildNumber/latestVersionCode/latestBuildNumber are coerced with bare `Number(data?.x ?? DEFAULT)`. A present-but-non-numeric server value (e.g. "v26", "26 pending", "N/A") is not nullish, so it survives the `??`, and `Number('v26')` yields NaN. That NaN flows into the gating comparisons.
src/services/appConfigService.ts.rootCause: No Number.isFinite validation after Number() coercion of admin-entered fields.
src/services/appConfigService.ts.failureScenario: Admin types a non-numeric value into minVersionCode. normalizeConfig sets minVersionCode = NaN. In checkForUpdate (L263) and evaluateUpdate (L281), `currentVersionCode < minCode` becomes `n < NaN` === false, so despite forceUpdate=true the force block silently never fires and a build that was supposed to be blocked keeps running. Same NaN on latestVersionCode disables the soft 'update available' notice.
src/services/appConfigService.ts.fix: Add a finite-number helper and use it for all numeric fields, e.g. `const num = (v: unknown, d: number) => { const n = Number(v); return Number.isFinite(n) ? n : d; };` then `minVersionCode: num(data?.minVersionCode, DEFAULT_CONFIG.minVersionCode)`, `latestVersionCode: num(data?.latestVersionCode ?? data?.minVersionCode, DEFAULT_CONFIG.latestVersionCode)`, etc.

src/services/auth/facebookAuth.ts.whatsWrong: AccessToken.getCurrentAccessToken() returns a Facebook Graph OAuth access token (opaque, non-JWT). That value (data.accessToken) is handed to supabase.auth.signInWithIdToken({provider:'facebook'}), which requires an OpenID Connect id_token (a signed JWT), not an access token. Compare googleAuth.ts L195/L205 which correctly passes signInResult.data.idToken. Facebook's classic LoginManager.logInWithPermissions flow does not return an id_token at all (only iOS Limited Login exposes one via AuthenticationToken). So Supabase rejects every attempt.
src/services/auth/facebookAuth.ts.rootCause: Confusing Facebook's Graph access token with an OIDC id_token; signInWithIdToken accepts only the latter.
src/services/auth/facebookAuth.ts.failureScenario: User taps 'Continue with Facebook', completes the FB consent screen, and gets an error toast every single time — the sign-in can never succeed because the token type is wrong. The feature is 100% broken (currently masked only because it's disabled in the UI).
src/services/auth/facebookAuth.ts.fix: Do not pass AccessToken.accessToken. Obtain an OIDC id_token instead: on iOS use AuthenticationToken.getAuthenticationTokenIOS() (configuring a nonce), or route the Graph access token through a Cloud Function that performs the token exchange server-side and returns a Supabase session. If neither an id_token nor a backend exchange is available, this provider cannot use signInWithIdToken.

src/services/auth/facebookAuth.ts.whatsWrong: When result.isCancelled is true, a plain Error('User cancelled the login process') is thrown, caught by the outer catch, logged via console.error('Facebook Login Error', error), and re-thrown as a generic Error(error.message || 'Facebook Login failed'). There is no cancel guard analogous to the 'not available' guard at L98. A deliberate user cancel is therefore reported to the UI as a login FAILURE and pollutes the error log.
src/services/auth/facebookAuth.ts.rootCause: Cancellation modeled as an exception with no distinguishing type, and the catch block treats every non-'not available' error identically.
src/services/auth/facebookAuth.ts.failureScenario: User opens the FB sheet, changes their mind, taps 'Cancel'. Instead of silently returning to the login screen, they see a red 'Facebook Login failed' error toast, and an error is written to the console/crash reporter for a completely normal action.
src/services/auth/facebookAuth.ts.fix: Add a cancel guard before the console.error, mirroring the 'not available' one: `if (error?.message?.includes('cancel')) throw error;` — or better, throw a typed CancelledError the caller can silently swallow. Also skip console.error for the cancel path.

src/services/auth/facebookAuth.ts.whatsWrong: The supabase.from('users').upsert({...}) result is awaited but its { error } is never destructured or checked. On an RLS denial, offline/timeout, or constraint violation the row write fails silently and the function still returns the in-memory `profile` at L96 as though the account row exists.
src/services/auth/facebookAuth.ts.rootCause: Fire-and-forget mutation whose error channel is ignored.
src/services/auth/facebookAuth.ts.failureScenario: Slow/no network (typical on Iraqi mobile) or an RLS policy mismatch: the users-row upsert rejects, but signInWithFacebook resolves successfully and the app treats the user as onboarded. Later screens that assume a persisted users row (orders/addresses FKs, profile fetch) break or write orphaned records, with zero error surfaced at sign-in time.
src/services/auth/facebookAuth.ts.fix: const { error: upsertError } = await supabase.from('users').upsert({...}); if (upsertError) throw upsertError; (at minimum log it and surface a warning).

src/services/auth/facebookAuth.ts.whatsWrong: signInWithFacebook has no in-flight guard. Two rapid taps invoke LoginManager.logInWithPermissions concurrently; the native SDK rejects the second with 'Login already in progress', which is caught and surfaced as a generic 'Facebook Login failed'. The two flows also race on getCurrentUserFresh()/upsert, potentially double-creating or clobbering the profile row.
src/services/auth/facebookAuth.ts.rootCause: No re-entrancy protection on an async auth entry point.
src/services/auth/facebookAuth.ts.failureScenario: Impatient user double-taps the Facebook button on a laggy 320dp device: the first login proceeds while the second throws, showing a spurious failure toast even though login actually succeeds; profile upsert may run twice.
src/services/auth/facebookAuth.ts.fix: Add a module-level guard: `let inFlight: Promise<User> | null = null;` at the top of signInWithFacebook `if (inFlight) return inFlight;` then `inFlight = (async () => { ... })().finally(() => { inFlight = null; }); return inFlight;`

src/services/auth/googleAuth.ts.whatsWrong: The very first statement of the catch block calls console.error with `fullError: JSON.stringify(error)` (line 260) with no guard. `error` is typed `any` and comes from a native module (google-signin) / Supabase. JSON.stringify throws a TypeError on any value containing a circular reference or a BigInt. Because this is the first line of the catch, the throw aborts the entire error-classification logic below it (statusCodes mapping, DEVELOPER_ERROR/12500 detection) before any of it runs.
src/services/auth/googleAuth.ts.rootCause: Serializing an untrusted native error object eagerly and unguarded at the top of the error handler.
src/services/auth/googleAuth.ts.failureScenario: A real Android DEVELOPER_ERROR (code 10) fires but the native error object carries a circular ref (common in RN native error bridges, e.g. nativeStackAndroid/nested cause). JSON.stringify throws 'Converting circular structure to JSON'. signInWithGoogleNative's catch itself throws this new error, so it reaches signInWithGoogle's catch (line 329) where `configProblem` no longer matches ('circular structure' contains none of the sentinel strings). Result: the web-OAuth fallback that SHOULD run for a config error never fires, and the user is shown a cryptic 'Converting circular structure to JSON' instead of the friendly misconfig message or a working fallback.
src/services/auth/googleAuth.ts.fix: Guard the stringify: `let fullError = ''; try { fullError = JSON.stringify(error); } catch { fullError = String(error?.message ?? error); }` and log `fullError`, or drop the JSON.stringify entirely and log `error` directly (console.error already prints objects). Never let the log line throw before error classification runs.

src/services/auth/googleAuth.ts.whatsWrong: Both profile-creation upserts `await supabase.from('users').upsert({...})` discard the returned `{ error }` — it is never destructured or checked. The function then returns a fully-populated User object as if the row were persisted.
src/services/auth/googleAuth.ts.rootCause: Fire-and-forget write: Supabase returns errors in the resolved value (does not throw), so an unchecked upsert swallows failures.
src/services/auth/googleAuth.ts.failureScenario: On a slow/dropping Iraqi mobile connection, supabase.auth.signInWithIdToken succeeds (creates the auth user) but the follow-up upsert to the `users` table times out or is rejected by RLS. The upsert error is ignored, so signInWithGoogleNative returns a valid User and the app logs the user straight in. No `users` row exists. On the next app open, getCurrentUserFresh sees PGRST116 (no row) and returns null, kicking the user back to the login screen — the classic 'it doesn't save my account' bug, with a now-orphaned auth account that can never re-run this new-user branch (signInWithIdToken will keep matching the existing auth user but the row is still missing).
src/services/auth/googleAuth.ts.fix: Check the error and fail loudly so the caller can retry: `const { error: upsertErr } = await supabase.from('users').upsert({...}); if (upsertErr) throw upsertErr;` in both signInWithGoogleNative (line 236) and buildProfileFromSession (line 56).

src/services/auth/phonePasswordAuth.ts.whatsWrong: The `supabase.from('users').upsert({...})` result is not destructured or checked — its `{ error }` is discarded. If the profile write fails, registration still returns success via `getCurrentUserFresh()` (L38) or the fallback object (L43-47).
src/services/auth/phonePasswordAuth.ts.rootCause: Missing error capture on the Supabase write; the function's success is decided by the session existing, not by the profile row actually persisting.
src/services/auth/phonePasswordAuth.ts.failureScenario: An Iraqi/OTPIQ admin finishes registration on flaky 3G. `supabase.auth.updateUser` (L28) succeeds but the subsequent `.upsert` times out. Because its error is ignored, the function reports success, yet the `users` row (name, phone, language — and `role:'admin', is_admin:true` from the L36 spread) was never written. The account has no name and, for admins, no admin flag, while the app believes registration succeeded.

src/services/auth/phonePasswordAuth.ts.whatsWrong: `supabase.from('users').update({ role: 'admin', is_admin: true }).eq('id', user.uid)` ignores both its `{ error }` and its matched-row count, then unconditionally sets `user.role='admin'`/`user.isAdmin=true` locally (L63-64) and returns that object.
src/services/auth/phonePasswordAuth.ts.rootCause: Local mutation of the returned User is treated as the source of truth while the DB write is fire-and-forget; no check that the write succeeded or matched a row.
src/services/auth/phonePasswordAuth.ts.failureScenario: A new admin registers via the synthetic-email path. The role UPDATE fails (RLS/network) or matches zero rows (row not yet visible after signUp). The returned object still says isAdmin=true, so the current session shows admin UI — but the DB row stays `customer`. On the next `getCurrentUserFresh()` or app restart the admin silently loses all admin access.

src/services/auth/securityService.ts.whatsWrong: reloadUser() intends to 'keep last-known cache on transient failure', but that only holds if getUser() throws. In supabase-js v2, supabase.auth.getUser() does NOT throw on a network error — it resolves to { data: { user: null }, error }. So the catch never fires; the success path runs `cachedUser = data?.user ?? null`, wiping the cached user to null on any offline/transient failure. This also cannot distinguish a genuine signed-out session (which SHOULD clear) from a network hiccup (which should NOT).
src/services/auth/securityService.ts.rootCause: Guard placed in catch{} instead of inspecting the returned `error`; gotrue-js returns errors in the result object rather than throwing.
src/services/auth/securityService.ts.failureScenario: User on Account & Security (has password + Apple linked) loses connectivity in transit. A screen focus effect runs reloadUser().then(refreshUser). getUser() returns { data:{ user:null }, error: FetchError } (no throw). cachedUser becomes null. getAuthState() now yields { email:null, hasPassword:false, hasApple:false, providers:[], providerCount:0 } — the screen renders the account as having no email and no sign-in methods, and getBestReauthMethod() returns 'signout' (hasPassword false), forcing a full sign-out reauth instead of the password prompt. Persists until the next successful reload.

src/services/bannerService.ts.whatsWrong: reorderBanners awaits `supabase.from('banners').update({ sort_order: i }).eq('id', id)` inside the loop but never inspects the returned `error`. The supabase-js query builder resolves with a `{ data, error }` object on PostgREST/RLS/HTTP failures — it does NOT reject/throw — so the surrounding try/catch is blind to per-row failures. The function returns `true` (success) even when some or all updates failed.
src/services/bannerService.ts.rootCause: Assuming `await` on a Supabase update rejects on failure (like fetch on a thrown error). It does not; failures are carried in the resolved `error` field, which is discarded here. Only genuine JS exceptions (rare) reach the catch.
src/services/bannerService.ts.failureScenario: Admin drags to reorder 5 banners. RLS or a transient 500 blocks the update on the 3rd id (or the app is backgrounded and the connection drops after row 2). The loop keeps going, no error is thrown, and reorderBanners returns true. The UI shows 'saved', but sort_order is now inconsistent — e.g. two banners share order 0 or the tail keeps stale values — so on next getBanners() the carousel renders in the wrong/duplicated order with no error surfaced to the admin.
src/services/bannerService.ts.fix: Check each update's error and abort/report on failure, e.g.: `for (let i = 0; i < orderedIds.length; i++) { const { error } = await supabase.from('banners').update({ sort_order: i }).eq('id', orderedIds[i]); if (error) throw error; }` — or better, batch via a single `upsert(orderedIds.map((id, i) => ({ id, sort_order: i })))` and check its returned error so a partial write is reported as failure (return false).

src/services/brandService.ts.whatsWrong: readMock() guards JSON.parse against throwing but never validates that the parsed value is an ARRAY. `if (raw) return JSON.parse(raw)` returns whatever was stored. If the AsyncStorage value for '@asankary_brands_mock_v5' is any valid-JSON non-array (e.g. '{}' from an aborted migration, manual tampering, or a partial/corrupt write), JSON.parse succeeds so the try/catch does NOT catch it, and the object is returned typed as Brand[].
src/services/brandService.ts.rootCause: try/catch only protects against parse THROWING; a successfully-parsed object/number/null passes through unvalidated because the code trusts the stored shape.
src/services/brandService.ts.failureScenario: Storage key holds the string '{}' (or 'null', or '42'). getActiveBrands() calls readMock() → returns {} → then `brands.filter(b => b.isActive)` throws 'brands.filter is not a function'. The Home 'Our Brands' section crashes on mount (and getAllBrands/saveBrand/deleteBrand crash the same way via .sort/.findIndex/.push). No fallback to SEED_BRANDS ever runs because the catch block is bypassed.
src/services/brandService.ts.fix: Validate the shape before returning: `if (raw) { const parsed = JSON.parse(raw); if (Array.isArray(parsed)) return parsed; }` — falling through to the seed-write + SEED_BRANDS.slice() path when parsed is not an array.

src/services/chatbotService.ts.whatsWrong: getActiveProductCatalog() destructures only `data` from the Supabase queries (line 999 and 1006) and ignores `error`. supabase-js does NOT throw on query/network failure — it resolves with {data: null, error}. On a transient failure both the is_active query and the fallback query return data=null, so `products` becomes `[]` and this empty array is written to catalogCache with a fresh timestamp (line 1010). For the next CATALOG_CACHE_TTL_MS (60s) every product lookup returns this cached empty catalog.
src/services/chatbotService.ts.rootCause: The `error` field is never inspected; a failed fetch is treated as an empty store and cached identically to a genuinely-empty store.
src/services/chatbotService.ts.failureScenario: User on a slow/flaky Iraqi mobile network asks 'do you have a battery for X'. The catalog SELECT times out at the network layer (data=null, error set). The code caches []. For the next 60 seconds — even after the network fully recovers — searchProductsByMessage/findProductsByPartNumbers all read the cached [] and buildProductContext appends the [PRODUCT_NOTE] 'No matching products were found', so the AI confidently tells the customer the store has no matching products when it actually does.

src/services/credentialStorage.ts.whatsWrong: clearCredentials runs three storage operations as sequential awaits under a single try/catch that silently swallows errors. If the FIRST await — SecureStore.deleteItemAsync(CREDENTIALS_KEY) — rejects, execution jumps straight to the empty catch and the two AsyncStorage.removeItem calls (lines 65 and 67) never run. SecureStore is Keystore/Keychain-backed and CAN reject in the field (Android keystore corruption, 'Could not decrypt', device migration, biometric/keystore invalidation). The comment 'Silently fail - credentials clearing is not critical' is wrong: this is the logout/clear path.
src/services/credentialStorage.ts.rootCause: Non-atomic sequential awaits sharing one try/catch; a rejection from any earlier op skips all later cleanup, and the catch discards the failure instead of best-effort continuing.
src/services/credentialStorage.ts.failureScenario: User taps Logout on a low-RAM Android after an OS update invalidated the keystore. clearCredentials() is called; SecureStore.deleteItemAsync throws → catch swallows it → REMEMBER_ME_KEY stays 'true' and the encrypted email+password stay on disk. On next launch, isRememberMeEnabled() returns true and the previous user's stored credentials are still retrievable via getCredentials() — the 'logged out' account was never actually cleared. Also the reverse-order fragility: any single op's rejection blocks the others.

src/services/firebase.ts.whatsWrong: handleFirebaseError dereferences error.code and error.message with no null/undefined guard. An error handler is exactly where unpredictable values arrive.
src/services/firebase.ts.rootCause: error is typed `any` and assumed to always be a Firebase error object; a rejected promise from a native Firebase module can settle with null/undefined, and code elsewhere can `throw` a non-Error value.
src/services/firebase.ts.failureScenario: A caller does `.catch(e => handleFirebaseError(e))` on an operation whose native module rejects with undefined (or code throws `throw null`). handleFirebaseError itself then throws `TypeError: Cannot read property 'code' of null`, masking the original error and crashing an otherwise-safe catch block. Currently latent because the function has no callers.
src/services/firebase.ts.fix: const errorCode = error?.code; const errorMessage = error?.message; (optionally `const error = maybeError ?? {};` at the top).

src/services/imageService.ts.whatsWrong: showImagePicker() wraps Alert.alert in a Promise and only resolves inside the Camera/Gallery/Cancel onPress handlers. On Android, Alert.alert is cancelable by default, so dismissing it with the hardware back button or a tap outside the dialog fires NONE of the onPress callbacks — so `resolve` is never called and the returned Promise never settles (neither resolves nor rejects). Called from 13 sites (ProfileScreen, AdminDashboardScreen, AdminProductsScreen, AdminStoreProfileScreen, AdminCategory/Brand/Settings screens, etc.), all as `await ImageService.showImagePicker()`.
src/services/imageService.ts.rootCause: Missing the Alert options object; Android's default cancelable dialog can dismiss without invoking any action button.
src/services/imageService.ts.failureScenario: An admin taps 'change logo', the 'Select Image' Alert appears, they change their mind and press the Android back button to dismiss it. No button handler runs, so the awaited promise hangs forever, leaking the suspended async frame and its resolve closure on every dismissal. Today's callers happen to set their loading flag AFTER the await (so no visible stuck spinner), but the promise-contract violation is a latent trap: any caller that sets an in-flight/loading guard BEFORE awaiting would hang with a permanent spinner and a disabled button.

src/services/phoneAuthService.ts.whatsWrong: normalizePhoneToE164 fabricates a valid-looking '+964' (or '+964<too-short>') for empty, whitespace-only, or all-non-digit input. There is no minimum-length / digit-count validation before prepending the country code. On line 11 `digits` can be '' and line 12 yields `local = ''`, so line 13 returns the string '+964'.
src/services/phoneAuthService.ts.rootCause: The final fallback branch unconditionally prepends '+964' to whatever survives digit-stripping, with no length floor for a real Iraqi mobile (which is 10 national digits, e.g. +9647XXXXXXXXX).
src/services/phoneAuthService.ts.failureScenario: In SignInScreen the phone field passes the `!phone.trim()` guard for any non-blank string. A user who types a single '0' (or '00', or a stray '.') reaches line 391 where `cleanPhone = '0'.replace(/\D/g,'').replace(/^0+/,'')` = '', so `formattedPhone = '+964'`, then checkPhoneExists('+964') → normalizePhoneToE164 returns '+964'. The RPC finds no match, the user is routed to Create-Account, and an account is persisted with phone '+964'. Worse, if any account already holds '+964', a different user can be matched to it.

src/services/phoneNumberService.ts.whatsWrong: detectCountryFromPhone and the auto-detect branch of stripCountryCode iterate COUNTRIES in declaration order and return/strip on the FIRST phoneCode that is a prefix of the cleaned digits. The list is not sorted longest-code-first, '+1' is duplicated (US at line 487 precedes CA at 506), and '+7' (Russia) is a single digit — so matching is ambiguous and order-dependent.
src/services/phoneNumberService.ts.rootCause: Linear first-prefix match over an unsorted, unanchored code list; single/short codes ('+1','+7') and duplicate '+1' make the first hit arbitrary.
src/services/phoneNumberService.ts.failureScenario: 1) detectCountryFromPhone('+1 416 555 1234') (a valid Canadian number) returns 'US', never 'CA' — and since the country drives currency (US=USD vs CA=CAD in the same data file) the wrong currency/format can be selected. 2) stripCountryCode('7501234567') — a bare Iraqi mobile local number with no country code passed — matches Russia's '+7' first and returns '501234567', silently corrupting the phone number used for OTP/WhatsApp contact. 3) Any Iraqi/Iranian bare local starting with a digit that collides with a short code is mis-stripped.
src/services/phoneNumberService.ts.fix: Only treat leading digits as a country code when the user actually typed one: `if (!phone.trim().startsWith('+')) return null;` (detect) / return cleaned unchanged (strip). Then match longest code first: `const sorted=[...COUNTRIES].sort((a,b)=>b.phoneCode.replace(/\D/g,'').length-a.phoneCode.replace(/\D/g,'').length);` and iterate that. US↔CA remain genuinely ambiguous under +1, so document that detect returns the first +1 country by design.

src/services/safeCallFunction.ts.whatsWrong: The network-failure detection matches on error.message containing 'Failed to fetch' or 'Network request failed', but supabase-js v2 (v2.106.2 installed) never surfaces those strings. On a real network failure, invoke returns a FunctionsFetchError whose .message is the FIXED string 'Failed to send a request to the Edge Function' (the underlying RN 'Network request failed' is stored on error.context, not error.message). So this condition is never true for the library actually in use — the friendly, user-facing message on line 19 is dead code and never fires.
src/services/safeCallFunction.ts.rootCause: Detection strings were written against raw fetch/browser error messages, not against supabase-js FunctionsFetchError, which overrides .message with a fixed string and hides the original error in .context.
src/services/safeCallFunction.ts.failureScenario: A shopper in Iraq with no/slow signal calls a function through safeCallFunction (e.g. checkout, chat, OTP). invoke resolves with error = FunctionsFetchError (message 'Failed to send a request to the Edge Function'). Line 18 does not match, so line 21 re-throws the raw error and the UI shows the opaque, untranslated English string 'Failed to send a request to the Edge Function' instead of the intended translatable 'Network error. Please check your connection.' — defeating the entire purpose of this wrapper for the most common failure mode.

src/services/settingsService.ts.whatsWrong: updateBusinessInfo/updateOperatingHours do a read-modify-write: they SELECT the current `data` JSON, spread it as the merge base, then UPSERT — which REPLACES the entire `data` column. But the SELECT destructures ONLY `{ data: existingData }` and silently ignores its `error`. supabase-js returns the error via {data,error} (it does not throw), so on ANY read failure `existingData` is null and `existingData?.data || {}` collapses the merge base to `{}`. A partial update then overwrites the whole document with just the new fields.
src/services/settingsService.ts.rootCause: The SELECT error is not inspected, and the code cannot distinguish 'no row yet' (PGRST116, legitimately empty base) from 'read failed, current doc unknown'. Combined with upsert replacing the full JSON blob, an unknown-current-state read becomes a full overwrite.
src/services/settingsService.ts.failureScenario: Admin in Iraq on a spotty mobile connection has business info saved with {name, address, phone, email, mapUrl}. They edit only the phone: updateBusinessInfo({phone:'...'}). At that instant the SELECT read times out/fails -> error ignored, existingData=null -> newData = {phone, updatedAt}. The upsert then succeeds (retry/network recovers), overwriting the row so name/address/email/mapUrl are PERMANENTLY lost. Same pattern lets two admins (or a double-tapped Save against interleaved reads) drop each other's fields.

src/services/tenantInfoService.ts.whatsWrong: DEFAULT_CONTACT is built from BRAND.contactPhone / BRAND.contactEmail, which in constants/config.ts are literal placeholders 'TODO_CONTACT_PHONE' and 'TODO_CONTACT_EMAIL'. This is the return value for EVERY fallback path: missing tenantId (line 22), query error, tenant-not-found, and mock mode (line 41). These placeholder strings are surfaced to the user as a real phone/whatsapp/email.
src/services/tenantInfoService.ts.rootCause: The service treats the BRAND TODO placeholders as valid contact data and never distinguishes 'not configured' from a real value.
src/services/tenantInfoService.ts.failureScenario: Tenant lookup fails or order has no tenantId. getTenantContactInfo returns whatsapp='TODO_CONTACT_PHONE'. In OrderDetailScreen.handleContactSupport (line 204) the guard `tenantContact?.whatsapp || '9647701279797'` does NOT rescue it — 'TODO_CONTACT_PHONE' is truthy, so it is used verbatim, producing `whatsapp://send?phone=TODO_CONTACT_PHONE`. User taps Contact Support and WhatsApp opens on a dead/invalid number (email/phone equally broken elsewhere).
src/services/tenantInfoService.ts.fix: Either fill real values in constants/config.ts, or normalize placeholders to undefined in this service so the caller's fallback engages: e.g. build DEFAULT_CONTACT with a helper `const real = (v?: string) => (v && !v.startsWith('TODO_') ? v : undefined);` and set phone/whatsapp/email via real(BRAND.contactPhone) etc. (name can keep 'Asankary').

src/services/videoService.ts.whatsWrong: VIDEO_CONFIG.MAX_DURATION_SECONDS (60s) is only passed as `videoMaxDuration` to launchImageLibraryAsync (L69), which reliably limits camera *recording*, not gallery selection — especially on Android where it is effectively ignored for library picks. validateVideo (L111-137) checks ONLY file size and never inspects duration, even though VideoPickResult already carries `duration`. So the advertised 60s cap is not actually enforced.
src/services/videoService.ts.rootCause: Duration limit relies on a picker option that doesn't govern library selection, and the client validator omits a duration check.
src/services/videoService.ts.failureScenario: An admin on a slow Iraqi mobile connection selects a 4-minute, 45MB product clip from the gallery. It passes validateVideo (under 50MB), then gets pushed through the 5-minute XHR upload, burning data and time, and may still be rejected server-side after the entire file has uploaded.
src/services/videoService.ts.fix: Enforce duration client-side: in validateVideo (or right after pickVideoFromGallery) compare the picked asset's duration (seconds) against VIDEO_CONFIG.MAX_DURATION_SECONDS and return { valid:false, error:`Video length exceeds ${MAX_DURATION_SECONDS}s` } before upload. E.g. pass duration into validateVideo and add: `if (duration != null && duration > VIDEO_CONFIG.MAX_DURATION_SECONDS) return { valid:false, error:t(...) };`

src/services/videoService.ts.whatsWrong: Upload Content-Type is `blob.type || 'video/mp4'` (L178, sent at L232). On Android, `fetch(fileUri).blob()` very commonly returns an empty `blob.type` for local file:// URIs, so the header silently defaults to video/mp4 regardless of the real format. The pick result also force-labels any `asset.type==='video'` as 'video/mp4' (L94), discarding the true mime.
src/services/videoService.ts.rootCause: Content-type derived from an unreliable blob.type with an mp4 fallback and no extension-based inference.
src/services/videoService.ts.failureScenario: A Kurdish admin on a Samsung device picks a .mov (or .webm) product clip. blob.type is '' → uploaded to BunnyCDN tagged video/mp4. Players/CDN that trust the stored content-type may refuse to play or mis-handle the clip.
src/services/videoService.ts.fix: Fall back to an extension-based mime when blob.type is empty, e.g. derive from the file extension of videoUri: `const ext = videoUri.split('.').pop()?.toLowerCase(); const byExt = ext==='mov' ? 'video/quicktime' : ext==='webm' ? 'video/webm' : 'video/mp4'; const contentType = blob.type || byExt;` and carry the same logic into pickVideoFromGallery's `type`.

src/ui/patchText.ts.whatsWrong: textBreakStrategy is placed inside the STYLE object (androidFixes) and merged into props.style. But textBreakStrategy is a Text PROP, not a TextStyle field — React Native silently ignores it when it appears in `style`. The inline comment calls this the 'CRITICAL ... main fix for Bold Text accessibility', yet it does absolutely nothing. The entire reason the patch exists (preventing bold/Arabic text cutoff in row layouts via 'simple' break strategy) never takes effect.
src/ui/patchText.ts.rootCause: Confusing a Text prop with a TextStyle property; style-array merge cannot carry props.
src/ui/patchText.ts.failureScenario: On a 320dp Android device with system Bold Text enabled, an Arabic label inside a horizontal row (e.g. a product-card price/title row) still uses the default 'highQuality' break strategy and clips exactly as before the patch was written — the developer believes it's fixed but it is not.
src/ui/patchText.ts.fix: Move it out of style and onto the prop, respecting any caller override: in the android branch add `patchedProps.textBreakStrategy = (props as any).textBreakStrategy ?? 'simple';` and DELETE the `textBreakStrategy: 'simple',` line from androidFixes.

src/ui/patchText.ts.whatsWrong: `allowFontScaling: true` is set AFTER `...props`, so it unconditionally overrides any caller that passed allowFontScaling={false}. Components that deliberately opt out of font scaling (fixed-width price/number badges, the AppNumber component, OTP boxes) are forced back into scaling globally, with no way to disable it.
src/ui/patchText.ts.rootCause: Hardcoding a value after the spread instead of falling back to the caller's value.
src/ui/patchText.ts.failureScenario: At max OS font size (200-300%), a price like `$1,299` rendered in a fixed-width amber badge with allowFontScaling={false} in source is force-scaled by this patch, overflowing/clipping the badge and breaking the row layout — the opposite of what the source intended.

src/ui/patchView.ts.whatsWrong: The patch computes safeStyles = { minHeight: flatStyle.height } and merges it via StyleSheet.flatten([props.style, safeStyles]), which KEEPS the original fixed `height` and adds an equal `minHeight`. In Yoga, a node with a fixed `height` resolves to exactly that height (clamped to minHeight, which is identical), so the container cannot grow. The comment at L40-41/55-56 ('so text can push the container to expand') is false — the patch has zero layout effect and does NOT prevent the clipping it exists to fix.
src/ui/patchView.ts.rootCause: minHeight only raises the lower bound; a present fixed `height` overrides it. To let content expand a container you must REMOVE the fixed height, not add an equal minHeight alongside it.
src/ui/patchView.ts.failureScenario: Samsung / max OS font size / Arabic RTL: a chip or badge styled { height: 36, overflow: 'hidden' } containing Arabic text. Patch yields { height: 36, minHeight: 36 } -> box stays locked at 36px -> Arabic text (taller line box, includeFontPadding) still clips at the bottom. The Samsung text-clipping bug this whole file targets is not actually fixed.
src/ui/patchView.ts.fix: Convert the fixed height into a floor and drop the hard height, e.g.: const { height, ...rest } = flatStyle; const patchedProps = { ...props, style: { ...rest, minHeight: height } }; (equivalently set height: undefined and minHeight: flatStyle.height). Only then can the container grow with scaled/RTL text.
